detailed_findings.finding: The map Phi(t)=I(t+1)-1 is indeed a bijection on {1,...,p-2}; one small implicit point is that I(t+1) ≠ 1 because t+1 ≠ 1, so the image really lies in {1,...,p-2}.

reason: The proof gives a coherent and complete argument for the stated residue-class case p ≡ 7 (mod 8). The bijection t ↦ I(t+1)-1 correctly transfers the condition I(k+1) < I(k) to t + I(t) < p-2, and the counting argument for {u : u + I(u) < p} via pairing u with p-u is valid once u + I(u) = p is excluded using p ≡ 3 (mod 4). The remaining exclusions at sums p-2 and p-1 are handled correctly, yielding |T| ≥ (p-5)/2 ≥ floor(p/4). No substantive semantic drift is present.
